headline: Northrop Grumman wins big. SpaceX stays busy.
deck: This week saw significant contracts and funding in the space sector.

stories.head: Northrop Grumman cashes in with $398M deal
stories.body: The Space Force awarded Northrop Grumman a substantial $398 million contract for satellite services, reinforcing their position in the lucrative military satellite market. This deal comes amid ongoing discussions about budget cuts, suggesting that Northrop may be securing its future cash flows while they still can. Meanwhile, competitors are left to ponder how to fill the gap left by such a sizable award.
stories.soWhat: In a tightening budget environment, locking in big contracts now could be the difference between thriving and just surviving.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M amid defense boom
stories.body: True Anomaly successfully closed a $190 million Series C round, bringing their valuation to $1.6 billion. This funding will bolster their efforts in co-orbital security and space domain awareness, areas that the DoD is increasingly prioritizing. With defense spending on the rise, True Anomaly's timing couldn’t be better as they position themselves to capture a larger share of the market.
stories.soWhat: Investors are clearly betting on defense as the new gold rush, and True Anomaly is riding that wave well.

stories.head: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser clears design review
stories.body: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant for the DoD has cleared its critical design review, a key milestone that could pave the way for more government contracts. This vehicle aims to provide cargo and crew transport capabilities, potentially tapping into a market that’s looking for alternatives to traditional solutions. The successful review indicates that Sierra is on track to meet the growing demand for flexible space transport options.
stories.soWhat: If Sierra can deliver on its promises, it might just carve out a niche in a crowded market dominated by SpaceX.

watchlist.title: SpaceX's valuation scrutiny continues
watchlist.body: With SpaceX's secondary market valuation hitting $470 billion, investors will be watching closely for any signs of instability or overvaluation.

watchlist.title: Upcoming Mars communications RFP results
watchlist.body: NASA's final RFP for the Mars communications orbiter will reveal which players are serious about interplanetary communications.

watchlist.title: Potential shifts in SDA program funding
watchlist.body: As York Space navigates the reshaping of SDA programs, expect to see ripple effects on funding priorities across the sector.

watchlist.title: Hypersonic testing delays raise concerns
watchlist.body: With hypersonic glide-vehicle tests slipping for the third consecutive quarter, stakeholders will be reassessing timelines and expectations.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
